title: Stone Game
summary: Two players take turns claiming either end pile.

contractDetails.constraints: An even number of piles from 2 to 500. Each pile contains 1–500 stones. The total number of stones is odd.
contractDetails.output-checking: Exact typed equality of the returned bool.

statement: Two players take turns claiming either end pile. Alice moves first, and both play optimally to maximize their own total. Return whether Alice finishes with more stones than Bob.

examples.explanation: Alice can claim the larger end pile.
Alice can force the original even-index pile set, totaling 12.
The two original index parities total 11 and 8, and Alice can secure the larger total.

constraints: An even number of piles from 2 to 500. Each pile contains 1–500 stones. The total number of stones is odd.
hints: Conceptual: The remaining piles always form one interval.
Directional: Track the current player’s best advantage on an interval.
Implementation: Compare taking the left end and taking the right end. Subtract the opponent’s resulting advantage from each chosen pile.
complexityAnalysis: O(n²) time and O(n) auxiliary space for the interval-DP reference. The parity property of this input domain also admits a constant-time result.
